items.title: An order with card type 2 (Visa) is placed with 200 and listed in alice's orders
covers: What happens step 3: card type 2 -> 200
What should happen: orders with a known card type are placed as before
items.reason: The fix adds a card type check in front of order creation; the ticket requires known card types to be placed as before, and step 3 of the reproduction is exactly this order. A regression would block every checkout. The order must be saved, which the Ordering functional host cannot do, so this runs as API calls on the test stack.

items.title: Repeating alice's order with card type 99 answers 400 naming the card type and places no order
covers: What happens step 4: card type 99
What should happen: 4xx that says the card type is not known, no server error
What should happen: the order with an unknown card type is not placed
items.reason: This is the ticket's reproduction on the real stack: after a successful card type 2 order, the same order with card type 99 used to answer 500 with an empty body. A bad request must not create an order, so the case also checks alice's order list on the deployed services (Ordering API, database and event flow), which only the test stack can show.

items.title: An order with card type 99 answers 400 problem details with an error under CardTypeId
covers: What should happen: bad request (4xx) that says the card type is not known; no server error
items.reason: Card type 99 is the ticket's own unknown value. Before the fix it reached the domain and answered 500 with an empty body; the contract is a 400 that names the card type. The request is rejected before the order is saved, so the functional host (real Postgres seeded with card types 1..3) is the cheapest layer that runs the real endpoint and card type query.

items.title: An order with card type 4, just above the highest known card type, answers 400
covers: Unknown card type, just outside the upper end of the known ids 1..3
items.reason: The known card types are 1..3; 4 is the first id just outside the upper end, so it catches an off-by-one or a range check that trusts ids near the known ones. Rejected before saving, so functional.

items.title: An order with card type 0, just below the lowest known card type, answers 400
covers: Unknown card type, just outside the lower end of the known ids 1..3
items.reason: 0 is the default value of an omitted int and the first id just below the known range; a check that treats 0 as "not set, use a default" would place an order with no card type. Rejected before saving, so functional.

items.title: An order with a negative card type (-1) answers 400
covers: Unknown card type, negative id
items.reason: A negative id can never be a card type; it must also be answered as a bad request instead of failing in the domain or the database. Rejected before saving, so functional.

items.title: An order with card type 1 (Amex), the lowest known card type, is placed with 200
covers: What should happen: orders with a known card type are placed as before

items.reason: The ticket says orders with a known card type are placed as before; card type 1 is the lowest id the shop lists, so it catches a check that excludes the ends of the range (the mirror of TC-BUG-57-05). items.reason: TC-01 and TC-02 assert alice has 'exactly 1 order', but TC-07 and TC-08 place orders for alice on the same default stack and nothing fixes the run order or requires a fresh stack. Use a baseline N (N+1 after TC-01, still N+1 after TC-02) as TC-07/TC-08 do, or require these cases to run serially on a fresh default scenario.

TC-02 to TC-06 require the CardTypeId message to contain the submitted id (99/4/0/-1). The story only requires the answer to say the card type is not known; asserting the key CardTypeId plus 'not known' is enough. The id comes from the current wording ('Card type {id} is not known.').

Delete TC-BUG-57-03: TC-BUG-57-02 already exercises card type 99 and checks the same 400 problem response, while additionally verifying that no order is created. TC-BUG-57-04 through TC-BUG-57-06 retain functional-layer rejection coverage.
